review: The hymn is the song of the redeemed: 1:1–8 is Ps 137:1–4 with Ps 45:9 (הֵיכְלֵי שֵׁן) and Song 1:12, 2:1–8 is Rev 5:9–10 nearly verbatim (אַתָּה רָאוּי … כִּי נִשְׁחַטְתָּ וּקְנִיתָ), and 3:1–8 is Rev 5:12–13 with Rev 11:15.

1:5–8 keep the print's three separate comparisons (the ivory palaces, the sweet echo, the fragrance) rather than compressing them: the Hebrew uses הֵיכְלֵי שֵׁן from Ps 45:9, הֵד for the echo, and רֵיחַ with בֹּשֶׂם (Song 4:10) for the fragrance, so each image lands on its own line.

2:3–4 כִּי שִׁלַּמְתָּ הַמְּחִיר הַיָּקָר / דָּמְךָ עַל־הַצְּלָב — the Arabic splits the payment and the price across the two lines (the price / Your blood on the cross); the Hebrew keeps the enjambement so the couplet reads as one transaction, which is what Rev 5:9 says.

3:3–4 לָקַחַת אֶת־הַכָּבוֹד וְאֶת־ / הַגְּדֻלָּה — the Arabic divides וְالْـ / ـمَجْدَ across the printed line break; the Hebrew mirrors the break at the same syntactic seam (the object marker at the end of line 3), so the run-on is preserved without breaking a word.
